messages:
marco: Heads-up — after the runtime allocator change in PR #2198 we're seeing intermittent OOMs on the 80GB Dedicated nodes when running long-context workloads with FlashAttention + cuBLASLt fallback. Repro: batch=4, seq=2048, model=gpt-6b-qlora.

anya: ugh. saw a couple alerts. any flamegraphs or nvprof traces?

marco: grabbed a quick run. peak resident jumped to ~77.8GB before OOM. nvprof snapshot shows big transient workspace peaks during FFN(1) and Attention(2). snippets: 
```
[MEMORY SNAPSHOT]
FFN workspace: 6.2GB transient
FlashAtt workspace: 3.9GB (when used)
cuBLASLt GEMM workspace: 8.4GB (fallback path)
KV cache per-token: ~0.64KB/token
Total predicted at seq=2048,batch=4 => ~82GB
```

tash: important detail: allocator now preallocates a 16GB workspace pool per-device at startup (opt-in via env). Did we forget to cap per-request workspace sizing?

marco: I think the allocator growth heuristics are too aggressive for mixed kernel combos. When FlashAttention kernel is chosen it still reserves cuBLASLt workspace for some FFN codepaths. Kernel selection and workspace sizing aren't coordinated.

darren: two quick mitigation ideas: 1) soft cap workspace per-request (try 4GB) + fallback to streaming matmul, 2) reuse pinned buffers across attention & FFN to avoid double-alloc. Both doable.

olivia: adding data: profiling run with kernel debug on: 
```
RUNTIME_PROFILE: [
  {op: 'attn_fwd', kernel: 'flash', work: 4096MB},
  {op: 'ffn_gemm', kernel: 'cublasLt', work: 8192MB},
  {op: 'kv_write', kernel: 'memcpy', work: 0.3MB/token}
]
```
Not surprising peaks overlap when model executes fused attention+ffn pipelined ops.

anya: can we add a simple heuristic: if cuBLASLt workspace > X and FlashAtt chosen, force smaller batch or switch FFN to Triton kernel with lower workspace req? We already have a triton_ffi flag for smaller GEMMs.

marco: yes. Proposed quick patch: compute per-op workspace estimate at plan-time and then compute worst-case sum of concurrently live workspaces based on scheduling windows. If worst-case > device_free - safety_margin => try options in order: reduce batch, enable triton-ffn, limit flashatt workspace to min_wa or use attention streaming.

tash: sample config to enable experiment: 
```json
{
  "allocator": "mempool-v2",
  "mempool": {
    "prealloc_mb": 16384,
    "soft_cap_per_request_mb": 4096,
    "reclaim_interval_ms": 200
  },
  "kernel_policies": {
    "attention": ["flash", "triton", "fallback"],
    "ffn": ["triton", "cublasLt"]
  }
}
```

darren: note: setting prealloc high helps throughput but hides fragmentation and can push us to OOM with overlapping workspaces. soft_cap_per_request is our friend here. Also add eager_free for ephemeral temps right after use.

anya: we should also track KV cache growth: long context => KV dominates. Suggest tracking per-request KV footprint and refuse extremely large batch+seq combos unless dedicated reservation. Add quota signal to API.

marco: agreed. From the run: KV alone at seq=2048,batch=4 => ~33GB. So combined with transient workspaces we exceed 80GB. Key changes to test: 
- planner workspace-summing check + fallback order 
- soft_cap_per_request 4GB + eager_free 
- reuse tensor pool between attention & ffn ops 
- API quota/guard for KV heavy calls

olivia: I can run an A/B on staging with these toggles. planning to spin up 3 runs: baseline, soft_cap only, planner-check + reuse. ETA ~2 hours.

infra-bot: deploy job started for branch "workspace-planner" on staging (job=ci/allocator-eval, id=ci-7762). Logs: https://ci.internal/jobs/ci-7762

marco: thx. if staging looks good we can roll to canary on Dedicated next week. Also let's add an observability metric: per-model "peak_concurrent_workspace_mb" and an alert when > 70% device.

darren: one more caution: FlashAttention's reported workspace is config-dependent on block size and dtype. Make sure planner asks the kernel for its max_workspace(dtypes, seq) instead of trusting static table.

anya: I'll own the planner patch + tests. tagging @tash for allocator tweaks and @olivia for staging runs.

marco: sweet. assign jira: INF-1293 (workspace planner + allocator soft cap).

olivia: update after first run: soft_cap-only reduced OOMs but throughput dropped ~8%. planner+reuse kept throughput within 2% of baseline and no OOMs in 6 hour run. sharing perf logs in #perf-results. :tada:

marco: awesome, let's iterate and then put safe defaults in Dedicated configs.
